title: Dripper: Token-Efficient Main HTML Extraction with a Lightweight LM

problem.claim: High-quality main-content extraction from web pages is needed to construct large-scale training corpora.

gap.claim: Heuristic extractors lack semantic reasoning for heterogeneous modern web structures, while generative LLMs are impractical at web scale because of computational cost, limited context windows, and hallucination risks.

contributions.claim: Dripper reformulates web-content extraction as a constrained sequence-labeling task using small language models.
The work introduces WebMainBench, a benchmark containing 7,809 human-annotated pages across 5,434 unique domains and multiple languages.
The work demonstrates infrastructural value by pre-training a 1B model on a Dripper-curated 63B-token corpus and open-sourcing the Dripper-0.6B weights and codebase.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The constrained sequence-labeling approach reaches a throughput of 3.08 pages per second on a single A100 GPU.
Dripper-0.6B reportedly outperforms heuristics such as Trafilatura and rivals DeepSeek-V3.2, GPT-5, and Gemini-2.5-Pro in an efficiency-accuracy trade-off.
A 1B model pre-trained on the Dripper-curated corpus reportedly significantly outperforms baselines on downstream tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-quality web main-content extraction is positioned as a prerequisite for large-scale training corpora.
Existing heuristic and generative approaches are described as insufficient for combining semantic handling with web-scale efficiency.
Dripper addresses the gap through constrained sequence labeling with small language models and reports high throughput.
The work presents WebMainBench and reports competitive performance against heuristic and large-model baselines.
The authors report downstream gains from a Dripper-curated pre-training corpus and release model weights and code.

source_observation.claim: A constrained sequence-labeling formulation with a small language model is reported to avoid generative hallucinations while achieving 3.08 pages per second on one A100 GPU.

interpretation.claim: Constraining model outputs can make semantic extraction more operationally feasible at scale.

application.claim: For large-scale corpus construction, consider task formulations that limit generation when extraction structure is known.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported web-page extraction setting.

source_observation.claim: A model pre-trained on a 63B-token corpus curated with Dripper is reported to outperform baselines on downstream tasks.

interpretation.claim: Extraction quality may materially affect the usefulness of large pre-training corpora.

application.claim: Corpus pipelines should evaluate extraction quality as a potential contributor to downstream model performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the downstream tasks, baselines, or controls needed to isolate extraction quality as the cause of the gains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation metrics, data splits, or statistical results.
The abstract does not identify the multiple languages included in WebMainBench.
The abstract does not describe the downstream tasks, baselines, or pre-training controls.
The abstract does not provide implementation details beyond the stated model sizes, throughput, and corpus scale.
